title: Start and Restore GPU Workloads in Seconds with NVIDIA Snapshot | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA open-sourced Snapshot, a Kubernetes checkpoint/restore system that captures fully initialized CPU+GPU memory of inference workers so new replicas skip weight loading, compilation and CUDA-graph capture. On B200 with VAST NFS it restored vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT LLM replicas in 3.6–42.7s versus cold starts of ~1.5 to 19 minutes (8x–36x faster), with design partners Crusoe and Saturn Cloud reporting similar gains on HGX B300.

themes.theme: Cold start as a capacity bottleneck

insights.claim: Initializing an LLM inference replica (cold start) can take minutes, so available GPUs do not translate immediately into serving capacity during demand spikes or replica failures.
insights.speaker: Ron Kahn
insights.so_what: Cold-start latency forces operators to over-provision idle GPUs; faster restore raises effective GPU utilization and makes scale-to-zero viable.
insights.quote: Initializing an LLM workload—a process known as a cold start—can take minutes, delaying scaling and recovery.
insights.locator: When inference demand spikes or a replica fails

insights.claim: Compilation, autotuning and CUDA graph capture — not weight loading — dominate cold start for large MoE models: e.g. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on vLLM spent 784.54s of a 1110.65s cold start compiling/capturing versus 184.90s loading weights.
insights.speaker: Ron Kahn
insights.so_what: Faster storage alone won't fix cold starts; restoring initialized state (not just weights) is the lever — relevant for model-streaming/storage vendors' pitch.
insights.locator: Table 2 breaks down the cold-start time

insights.claim: NVIDIA Snapshot, an open-source DSX AI Factory component originally built for Dynamo workers, checkpoints a fully initialized GPU Pod's CPU and GPU memory as a portable artifact and restores it onto any node with the same GPU model and driver, skipping weight loading, compilation and graph capture.
insights.speaker: Ron Kahn
insights.so_what: Same-GPU-model-and-driver requirement favors homogeneous fleets and reinforces NVIDIA stack consistency.
insights.locator: Snapshot provides two operations for GPU Pods

insights.claim: Snapshot uses Kubernetes custom resources (PodSnapshot, SnapshotJob, and a nvidia.com/restore-from annotation), requires only a small pause/resume handshake in the workload, and ships examples for vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT LLM.
insights.speaker: Ron Kahn
insights.so_what: Engine-agnostic support means the benefit accrues to the whole open inference ecosystem running on NVIDIA GPUs.
insights.locator: Both operations use Kubernetes custom resources

insights.claim: Snapshot can checkpoint multi-GPU single-node workloads as one artifact across ranks, supporting large MoE models with tensor, data/expert and decode context parallelism.
insights.speaker: Ron Kahn
insights.so_what: Makes fast autoscaling practical for frontier-scale MoE serving, the costliest replicas to cold start.
insights.locator: Snapshot can checkpoint and restore compatible workloads

insights.claim: On NVIDIA B200 with VAST NFS storage, Snapshot restored inference replicas in 3.6 to 42.7 seconds across all tested vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT LLM configurations, 8x to 36x faster than cold start.
insights.speaker: Ron Kahn
insights.so_what: Order-of-magnitude faster scale-out improves inference economics for GPU clouds and token factories.
insights.quote: Snapshot restored replicas in 3.6 to 42.7 seconds—8x to 36x faster than cold start.

insights.claim: The largest MoE models, with checkpoints of about 600 GB to 1 TB across eight GPUs, restored in under 43 seconds compared with cold-start times of 6 to 19 minutes.
insights.speaker: Ron Kahn
insights.so_what: Biggest savings land on the largest models — where idle reserve capacity is most expensive.

insights.claim: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on vLLM (TEP8) went from a 1110.65s cold start to a 30.96s Snapshot restore, the top 35.87x speedup in the benchmark.
insights.speaker: Ron Kahn
insights.so_what: Concrete best-case figure for scale-from-zero of frontier open MoE models.
insights.locator: Table 1. Cold start compared with a Snapshot restore

insights.claim: In every tested configuration, checkpoint time plus restore time was shorter than a single cold start, with one-time checkpoint creation taking 15 seconds to 5.5 minutes.
insights.speaker: Ron Kahn
insights.so_what: Payback is immediate — no break-even hurdle to adoption.
insights.quote: Checkpointing pays off with the first restored replica
insights.locator: Checkpointing pays off with the first restored replica

insights.claim: Checkpoint artifacts are larger than weights — e.g. 1039.09 GB for DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4 on SGLang versus 913.09 GB of weights, and 693.89 GB for gpt-oss-120b SGLang TP4 versus 65.25 GB weights — implying significant storage demand.
insights.speaker: Ron Kahn
insights.so_what: Widespread snapshot adoption increases demand for high-throughput shared storage (e.g. VAST-type NFS) per model configuration.
insights.locator: Table 1. Cold start compared with a Snapshot restore

insights.claim: For eight-GPU MoE restores, copying GPU state back into GPU memory takes 18 to 29 seconds and dominates, while CRIU-based CPU process restore takes 4.2 to 10.8 seconds and is governed mostly by the storage backend.
insights.speaker: Ron Kahn
insights.so_what: Further restore gains depend on host-to-GPU bandwidth and storage throughput — the next bottlenecks to watch.
insights.quote: Moving GPU state dominates large restores
insights.locator: Moving GPU state dominates large restores

insights.claim: Crusoe, an upstream Snapshot contributor, cut GLM-5.3 Pod readiness from roughly 8 minutes to 31 seconds on NVIDIA HGX B300.
insights.speaker: Ron Kahn
insights.so_what: Neocloud adoption signals Snapshot may become a standard elasticity feature for GPU clouds.
insights.locator: Crusoe, an upstream contributor to Snapshot

insights.claim: Saturn Cloud, a token factory platform, cut vLLM startup for scale-from-zero inference from 2–8.5 minutes to 6–34 seconds on NVIDIA HGX B300 using Snapshot.
insights.speaker: Ron Kahn
insights.so_what: Scale-from-zero becomes practical, enabling serverless-style GPU inference pricing.
insights.locator: Saturn Cloud, a token factory platform
